# Kaizen Agent

> **Product-first AI team for manufacturing anomaly detection and root-cause tracing.**

Kaizen Agent is an autonomous multi-agent system built for small and mid-size factories in Southeast Asia. It watches finished products leaving the production line, detects quality defects the moment they appear, traces the defect back to its exact machine / tool / material / process root cause, guides the on-floor technician through the repair in their native language, and closes the incident only after the product itself confirms the fix — all in under 90 seconds.

The name comes from the Japanese manufacturing philosophy of *continuous improvement* (改善). The system is designed to embed that loop directly into real-time operations.

---

## Why product-first?

Most factory monitoring systems start from machine sensors. Kaizen Agent starts from the **product**.

A machine can be silently producing scrap for hours while every sensor reads "normal". Only the product tells the truth. By anchoring detection at the inspection station and working *backwards* through traceability data to the responsible machine and time window, the system narrows the root-cause search space before it ever queries a sensor — making analysis faster, more accurate, and independent of sensor coverage gaps.

---

## Architecture overview

The system is organised into four sequential phases, coordinated by a central **Orchestrator** built on Google ADK:

**Phase A — Detection**
A Gemma 3-powered edge gateway at the camera inspection station classifies product defects in real time and publishes anomaly events when the defect rate breaches the Statistical Process Control (SPC) upper control limit.

**Phase B — Tracing & Root Cause**
Three agents work in parallel:
- **Traceability Agent** — cross-references BigQuery discrete event logs to isolate which machine, tool, operator, and raw-material lot produced the defective parts.
- **Process Analyst Agent** — pulls telemetry (vibration, temperature, current) for only the suspect machine in the suspect time window.
- **Root Cause Agent** — synthesises 5-Whys and Ishikawa analysis using Vertex AI Search over maintenance logs, equipment manuals, and historical 8D reports.

**Phase C — Resolution**
The **Technician Copilot** opens a Gemini Live multimodal session — voice plus camera — guiding the technician through the repair procedure in Vietnamese (or any configured language). The **Incident Scribe** simultaneously generates a draft 8D report and corrective work order for human review.

**Phase D — Verification & Learning**
The **Quality Inspector** holds the incident open until *N* consecutive products pass the inspection gate. On closure, the **Continuous Learning Agent** indexes the resolution into the vector knowledge base and publishes a sustainability impact card (scrap avoided, downtime saved, energy and CO₂ reduction).

**Shared state** flows through a **Blackboard** (Firestore-backed) that all agents read from and write to, exposed to the dashboard via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

**Tech stack:** Python 3.11 · FastAPI · Google ADK · Gemini 2.0 · Gemma 3 Edge · Vertex AI Search · BigQuery · Firestore · Pub/Sub · React + Vite

---

## Quickstart

### Prerequisites
- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) — manages Python 3.11 and Node 22 automatically
- Google Cloud project with BigQuery, Firestore, and Vertex AI enabled (for production; mock data works locally without credentials)

### 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/kaizen-agent.git
cd kaizen-agent

mise install          # provisions Python 3.11 + Node 22 + .venv
mise run install      # pip install backend deps + npm install frontend deps
```

### 2. Configure environment

```bash
cp .env.example .env  # add your GCP_PROJECT_ID, etc.
```

Local development works without GCP credentials — the backend falls back to in-memory mock data automatically.

### 3. Run the full stack

```bash
# Backend (FastAPI on :8000) + Frontend (Vite on :3000) in parallel
mise run dev -j2
```

Or run each side independently:

```bash
mise run backend    # FastAPI with auto-reload
mise run frontend   # Vite dev server
```

### 4. Trigger the demo

With the backend running, inject a synthetic defect to see the full 90-second multi-agent incident loop:

```bash
mise run demo
```

Then open `http://localhost:8000` to watch the live dashboard.

### Other useful commands

```bash
mise run test        # run pytest
mise run seed        # seed mock BigQuery / Firestore data
mise run docker:up   # start via docker compose
```

---

## License

MIT © 2024 Kaizen Agent Contributors

# AGENTS.md — Kaizen Agent Contributor Guide

This file is the authoritative reference for AI coding agents and human contributors working on this repository. Read it before writing any code.

---

## Project Layout

```
.
├── backend/                    # Python — FastAPI server, AI agents, tools
│   ├── agents/                 # One file per ADK agent
│   │   ├── orchestrator.py     # State machine; coordinates all agents
│   │   ├── quality_inspector.py
│   │   ├── traceability.py
│   │   ├── process_analyst.py
│   │   ├── root_cause.py
│   │   ├── technician_copilot.py
│   │   ├── incident_scribe.py
│   │   └── continuous_learning.py
│   ├── api/                    # FastAPI routers
│   │   ├── main.py             # App factory, mounts routers
│   │   ├── routes_incidents.py # SSE stream + incident read endpoints
│   │   ├── routes_simulation.py# Demo inject / reset endpoints
│   │   └── routes_gemini_live.py
│   ├── core/                   # Shared primitives (import freely)
│   │   ├── models.py           # Pydantic schemas — single source of truth
│   │   ├── blackboard.py       # Reactive shared state (asyncio + SSE)
│   │   └── config.py           # Settings via pydantic-settings / .env
│   ├── edge/                   # Edge device code (Gemma classifier, MQTT bridge)
│   │   ├── gateway/
│   │   └── simulator/          # Local mock of edge hardware for dev
│   ├── tools/                  # Stateless ADK tool functions
│   │   ├── bigquery_tool.py    # Traceability + telemetry queries (+ mock seed)
│   │   ├── spc_calculator.py
│   │   ├── impact_calculator.py
│   │   └── rag_search_tool.py
│   └── requirements.txt
│
├── frontend/                   # React + Vite dashboard
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.jsx            # Entry point
│   │   ├── App.jsx             # Root component / router
│   │   ├── components/         # Reusable UI components
│   │   └── pages/              # Route-level page components
│   ├── public/
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── vite.config.js          # Dev proxy: /api → localhost:8000
│   └── package.json
│
├── data/
│   ├── datasets/               # Raw / mock sensor and traceability data
│   ├── knowledge_base/         # PDFs, maintenance logs, 8D reports for RAG
│   └── schemas/                # BigQuery DDL and Firestore schema definitions
│
├── docs/                       # Architecture diagrams (.mmd + rendered .svg)
├── tests/                      # pytest test suite (mirrors backend/ structure)
├── mise.toml                   # Tool versions + all dev tasks (canonical runner)
├── docker-compose.yml          # Local multi-service compose
├── .gitignore
├── README.md
└── AGENTS.md                   # ← this file
```

---

## Coding Conventions

### Python (backend/)

- **Style:** PEP 8, enforced via `ruff` (line length 100). Do not use `black` separately — `ruff format` handles formatting.
- **Type hints:** Required on all public functions and class methods. Use `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of every module.
- **Pydantic:** All data flowing between agents and the API **must** be defined as a Pydantic model in `backend/core/models.py`. Never define ad-hoc dicts for inter-agent data.
- **Async:** All agent logic and API handlers must be `async def`. Do not call blocking I/O inside coroutines — use `asyncio.to_thread` if necessary.
- **Imports:** Absolute imports only (`from backend.core.models import ...`). No relative imports (`from ..core`).
- **Module docstring:** Every file must open with a one-line `"""..."""` docstring describing its responsibility.
- **No print():** Use Python `logging` (`import logging; logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`). The `config.py` sets the log level from the environment.
- **Secrets:** Never hardcode credentials. All secrets come from environment variables via `backend/core/config.py` (pydantic-settings).

```python
# Good
from __future__ import annotations
"""Quality Inspector agent: detects SPC breaches and opens incidents."""

import logging
from backend.core.models import AgentFinding

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

async def inspect(defect_rate: float) -> AgentFinding:
    ...
```

### JavaScript / React (frontend/)

- **Style:** ESLint + Prettier (2-space indent, single quotes, no semicolons).
- **Components:** Functional components only — no class components. One component per file. File name matches the exported component name.
- **State:** Local `useState` / `useReducer` for UI-only state. Global incident state comes via the SSE hook — do not duplicate it in Redux/Zustand unless the app grows to need it.
- **API calls:** All `/api/*` calls are proxied by Vite in dev and by the server in prod. Never hardcode `localhost:8000` in component code — use relative paths.
- **Props:** Always destructure props in the function signature. Use PropTypes or JSDoc for public components.

```jsx
// Good
export default function SpcChart({ bars, ucl }) {
  return <canvas aria-label="SPC defect rate chart" />;
}
```

### General

- **No commented-out code** in commits. Use `git stash` or a feature branch instead.
- **Test coverage:** Any new function in `backend/tools/` or `backend/core/` must have a corresponding test in `tests/`.
- **Environment parity:** Code must work with mock data when `GCP_PROJECT_ID` is unset. Never assume live GCP services in local dev paths.

---

## Commit Convention

Follow **Conventional Commits** (`<type>(<scope>): <subject>`).

### Types

| Type | When to use |
|---|---|
| `feat` | New user-facing feature or agent capability |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `refactor` | Code restructuring with no behaviour change |
| `test` | Adding or updating tests |
| `docs` | Documentation only |
| `chore` | Tooling, deps, config (mise, gitignore, CI) |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `style` | Formatting, linting (no logic change) |

### Scopes

Use the top-level area affected: `backend`, `frontend`, `agents`, `api`, `core`, `edge`, `tools`, `data`, `docs`, `ci`.

### Examples

```
feat(agents): add process analyst vibration spike detection
fix(api): handle missing confidence field in LEARN agent finding
refactor(core): extract blackboard subscriber cleanup into context manager
test(tools): add unit tests for spc_calculator UCL logic
docs: update architecture overview in README
chore(mise): migrate all Makefile tasks to mise.toml
```

### Rules

- Subject line: imperative mood, lowercase, no trailing period, max 72 chars.
- Body (optional): explain *why*, not *what*. Reference issue numbers with `Fixes #123`.
- Breaking changes: add `!` after the type (`feat!:`) and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

---

## Branching Convention

```
main                  — production-ready; protected; merge via PR only
└── dev               — integration branch; all features merge here first
    ├── feat/<name>   — new features
    ├── fix/<name>    — bug fixes
    ├── refactor/<name>
    ├── chore/<name>  — tooling / config
    └── docs/<name>   — documentation only
```

### Rules

- Branch off `dev`, not `main`.
- Use kebab-case for branch names: `feat/traceability-batch-query`, `fix/sse-reconnect`.
- Keep branches short-lived. Merge or rebase within the same sprint.
- Delete the branch after merging.
- `main` only receives merges from `dev` via a reviewed PR. Direct pushes to `main` are blocked.

### PR checklist (before merging to dev)

- [ ] `mise run test` passes
- [ ] `mise run test:health` passes against a local server
- [ ] No secrets or hardcoded credentials
- [ ] New behaviour covered by a test
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` updated if conventions changed

---

## Key Invariants

Agents should never violate these:

1. **`backend/core/models.py` is the single schema source of truth.** All Pydantic models live here. Never define a competing schema elsewhere.
2. **The Blackboard is the only shared state bus.** Agents communicate exclusively by reading from and writing to `backend/core/blackboard.py`. No direct agent-to-agent calls.
3. **Incidents close on product evidence only.** The orchestrator transitions to `closed` only after `verification_count >= verification_target`. Do not shortcut this.
4. **Mock data must always work.** The `bigquery_tool.py` mock path must remain functional without any GCP credentials so local development never requires a live project.
5. **Frontend never calls backend directly by hostname.** All API calls use relative URLs (`/api/...`) so the Vite proxy (dev) and server (prod) handle routing transparently.

"""ADK Tool: Executes queries against BigQuery (or bigquery-emulator) for traceability and sensor telemetry."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import logging
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from backend.core.config import settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MOCK_TRACEABILITY_PATH = "data/datasets/mock_traceability.csv"
SCHEMA_SQL_PATH = "data/schemas/bigquery_tables.sql"

SEED_ROWS = [
    ["product_id", "timestamp", "machine_id", "tool_id", "lot_id", "operator_id", "status"],
    ["PRD-1001", "2026-10-05T09:20:00", "CNC-01", "T04", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-12", "PASS"],
    ["PRD-1002", "2026-10-05T09:25:00", "CNC-03", "T07", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-08", "PASS"],
    ["PRD-1003", "2026-10-05T09:35:00", "CNC-02", "T07", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-15", "PASS"],
    ["PRD-1004", "2026-10-05T09:40:00", "CNC-02", "T07", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-15", "DEFECT_SCRATCH"],
    ["PRD-1005", "2026-10-05T09:42:00", "CNC-02", "T07", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-15", "DEFECT_SCRATCH"],
    ["PRD-1006", "2026-10-05T09:44:00", "CNC-01", "T04", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-12", "PASS"],
    ["PRD-1007", "2026-10-05T09:45:00", "CNC-02", "T07", "AL-5083-B4", "OP-15", "DEFECT_SCRATCH"],
]


def get_bigquery_client() -> Optional[Any]:
    """Returns a BigQuery client targeting the emulator or GCP, or None if unavailable."""
    emulator_host = settings.bigquery_emulator_host or os.getenv("BIGQUERY_EMULATOR_HOST")

    try:
        from google.auth.credentials import AnonymousCredentials
        from google.cloud import bigquery

        if emulator_host:
            logger.info("Connecting to BigQuery Emulator at %s", emulator_host)
            endpoint = emulator_host if "://" in emulator_host else f"http://{emulator_host}"
            return bigquery.Client(
                project=settings.gcp_project_id,
                credentials=AnonymousCredentials(),
                client_options={"api_endpoint": endpoint},
            )

        if os.getenv("GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS") or os.getenv("GCP_PROJECT_ID"):
            return bigquery.Client(project=settings.gcp_project_id)

    except Exception as exc:
        logger.debug("BigQuery client initialization bypassed (%s); using in-memory mock", exc)

    return None


def seed_mock_data() -> None:
    """Generates mock traceability CSV and syncs to BigQuery/Emulator if connected."""
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(MOCK_TRACEABILITY_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    with open(MOCK_TRACEABILITY_PATH, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerows(SEED_ROWS)
    logger.info("Seeded mock traceability data at: %s", MOCK_TRACEABILITY_PATH)

    client = get_bigquery_client()
    if client:
        try:
            _sync_seed_to_bigquery(client)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("Could not sync seed data to BigQuery/Emulator: %s", exc)


def _sync_seed_to_bigquery(client: Any) -> None:
    """Creates dataset and table in BigQuery/Emulator and loads seed records."""
    from google.cloud import bigquery

    dataset_id = f"{client.project}.{settings.bigquery_dataset}"
    dataset = bigquery.Dataset(dataset_id)
    dataset.location = settings.gcp_region
    client.create_dataset(dataset, exists_ok=True)

    # Initialize schema DDL if file is available
    if os.path.exists(SCHEMA_SQL_PATH):
        with open(SCHEMA_SQL_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            ddl = f.read()
            for statement in ddl.split(";"):
                stmt = statement.strip()
                if stmt:
                    try:
                        client.query(stmt).result()
                    except Exception as exc:
                        logger.debug("DDL execution note: %s", exc)

    table_ref = f"{dataset_id}.traceability"
    rows_to_insert = [
        {
            "product_id": r[0],
            "timestamp": f"{r[1]}Z",
            "machine_id": r[2],
            "tool_id": r[3],
            "lot_id": r[4],
            "operator_id": r[5],
            "status": r[6],
        }
        for r in SEED_ROWS[1:]
    ]
    errors = client.insert_rows_json(table_ref, rows_to_insert)
    if errors:
        logger.warning("Errors inserting seed rows into BigQuery: %s", errors)
    else:
        logger.info("Successfully seeded %d rows into BigQuery/Emulator table %s", len(rows_to_insert), table_ref)


def query_traceability_topology(time_window: str = "09:30-10:00") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Queries discrete topology diff from BigQuery / Emulator, with graceful mock fallback."""
    client = get_bigquery_client()

    if client:
        try:
            dataset_id = f"{client.project}.{settings.bigquery_dataset}"
            query = f"""
                SELECT
                    machine_id,
                    tool_id,
                    COUNTIF(status LIKE 'DEFECT%') as defect_count,
                    COUNT(*) as total_parts,
                    SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(status LIKE 'DEFECT%'), COUNT(*)) as defect_ratio
                FROM `{dataset_id}.traceability`
                GROUP BY machine_id, tool_id
                ORDER BY defect_ratio DESC, defect_count DESC
            """
            results = client.query(query).result()
            suspects: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            for row in results:
                ratio = float(row.defect_ratio or 0.0)
                suspects.append({
                    "machine_id": row.machine_id,
                    "tool_id": row.tool_id,
                    "correlation_score": round(ratio, 2),
                    "defect_count": row.defect_count,
                    "total_parts": row.total_parts,
                })

            if suspects:
                return {
                    "source": "bigquery_emulator" if settings.bigquery_emulator_host else "bigquery_live",
                    "suspects": suspects,
                    "excluded_factors": ["lot_id: AL-5083-B4 (normal defect distribution across lots)"],
                }
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("BigQuery query failed (%s); falling back to mock topology", exc)

    # In-memory mock fallback (Key Invariant 4: Mock data must always work)
    return {
        "source": "mock_fallback",
        "suspects": [
            {"machine_id": "CNC-02", "tool_id": "T07", "correlation_score": 0.95},
            {"machine_id": "CNC-01", "tool_id": "T04", "correlation_score": 0.02},
            {"machine_id": "CNC-03", "tool_id": "T07", "correlation_score": 0.01},
        ],
        "excluded_factors": ["lot_id: AL-5083-B4 (normal on CNC-01/03)"],
    }

**Tech stack:** Python 3.11 · FastAPI · Google ADK · Gemini 2.0 · Gemma 3 Edge · Vertex AI Search · BigQuery / bigquery-emulator · Firestore · Pub/Sub · React + Vite + TypeScript

---

## Quickstart

### Prerequisites
- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) — manages Python 3.11 and Node 22 automatically
- Docker (optional, for running `goccy/bigquery-emulator` locally)
- Google Cloud project with BigQuery, Firestore, and Vertex AI enabled (for production; mock data works locally without credentials)

### 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/kaizen-agent.git
cd kaizen-agent

mise install          # provisions Python 3.11 + Node 22 + .venv
mise run install      # pip install backend deps + npm install frontend deps
```

### 2. Configure environment

Create a `mise.local.toml` at the repo root to set machine-local overrides (this file is gitignored):

```toml
# mise.local.toml — local secrets and overrides, never committed
[env]
GCP_PROJECT_ID                 = "your-gcp-project"
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS = "/absolute/path/to/service-account.json"
APP_ENV                        = "development"

# Optional: target local BigQuery emulator for dev parity without GCP
# BIGQUERY_EMULATOR_HOST       = "http://localhost:9050"
```

mise automatically merges `mise.local.toml` on top of `mise.toml` when you `cd` into the directory, so any task run via `mise run` will pick up these variables without extra shell exports.

Local development works without GCP credentials — start the local BigQuery emulator (`mise run emulator`) or leave it unset to automatically fall back to mock data.

### 3. Run the full stack

```bash
# Backend (FastAPI on :8000) + Frontend (Vite on :3000) in parallel
mise run dev -j2
```

Or run each side independently:

```bash
mise run backend    # FastAPI with auto-reload
mise run frontend   # Vite dev server
```

### 4. Trigger the demo

With the backend running, inject a synthetic defect to see the full 90-second multi-agent incident loop:

```bash
mise run demo
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000` (frontend) or `http://localhost:8000` (FastAPI backend) to watch the live dashboard.

### Other useful commands

```bash
mise run test           # run pytest
mise run seed           # seed mock BigQuery / Firestore data
mise run emulator       # start local BigQuery emulator (:9050)
mise run emulator:down  # stop BigQuery emulator
mise run docker:up      # start full stack via docker compose
```

Google Cloud SDK and the open-source ecosystem provide containerized emulators for each component in the Kaizen Agent stack. --- ### Dependency Emulation Matrix | Component | Role in Kaizen Agent | Recommended Docker Image | Default Port | Client / SDK Integration | |---|---|---|---|---| | **BigQuery** | Traceability topology, telemetry, & 8D impact metrics | `ghcr.io/goccy/bigquery-emulator:latest` | `9050` | `BIGQUERY_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:9050`
`google-cloud-bigquery` connects via `AnonymousCredentials()` | | **Firestore** | Blackboard shared reactive state bus | `gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators` | `8086` | `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:8086`
`google-cloud-firestore` auto-detects and connects with zero credentials | | **Cloud Pub/Sub** | Real-time event bus from camera & sensor edge gateway | `gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators` | `8085` | `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:8085`
`google-cloud-pubsub` auto-routes all publish/subscribe calls | | **MQTT Broker** | Factory floor conveyor & CNC telemetry bridge | `eclipse-mosquitto:latest` | `1883` | Standard MQTT protocol (`paho-mqtt` or edge gateway bridge) | | **Edge Gemma / Vision** | Local camera defect classification at inspection gate | `ollama/ollama:latest` *(Optional)* | `11434` | Serves `gemma:2b` or `gemma:7b` locally for offline edge inference | --- ### How SDKs Handle Emulators (Zero Code Changes) Official Google Cloud client libraries natively inspect the environment: 1. **Firestore:** When `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` is set, `firestore.Client()` automatically skips GCP OAuth authentication and connects via unencrypted HTTP to the emulator. 2. **Pub/Sub:** When `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST` is set, `pubsub_v1.PublisherClient()` and `SubscriberClient()` route to the local gRPC/HTTP endpoint. 3. **BigQuery:** When `BIGQUERY_EMULATOR_HOST` is configured, `bigquery.Client(credentials=AnonymousCredentials(), client_options={"api_endpoint": ...})` executes ANSI SQL queries locally against SQLite/in-memory storage inside the container. --- ### Proposed Unified `docker-compose.yml` Architecture ```yaml version: '3.8' services: # 1. **No, you do not need backend and frontend inside `docker-compose.yml`.** 

In fact, running **infrastructure/emulators in Docker** and your **application code natively via `mise`** is the recommended best practice for local development.

---

### Why keeping them outside Docker is better

| Benefit | Native via `mise run dev -j2` | Inside Docker Container |
|---|---|---|
| **Hot Reload & HMR** | **Instant** (Vite HMR & Uvicorn reload on macOS filesystem) | Noticeable lag due to Docker volume mount syncing |
| **IDE Debugging** | One-click breakpoints & debugger attach in VS Code / Antigravity | Requires remote debug ports & container mapping |
| **Build & Startup** | Zero seconds (code runs directly from your virtualenv/node) | Requires Docker rebuilds on dependency/code changes |
| **Resource Usage** | Lightweight (Docker only runs idle emulators in background) | Heavy (Docker runs Node, Python, plus all containers) |

---

### The Clean "Local Dev" Workflow

1. **Docker Compose handles the services you can't run natively:**
   - BigQuery emulator (`:9050`)
   - Firestore emulator (`:8086`)
   - Pub/Sub emulator (`:8085`)
   - Mosquitto MQTT broker (`:1883`)

2. **`mise` handles your application code:**
   - Backend runs on `http://localhost:8000` with instant auto-reload.
   - Frontend runs on `http://localhost:3000` with instant Vite HMR.
   - Both connect directly to `localhost` ports (`localhost:9050`, `localhost:8086`, etc.).

---

### Recommended Clean `docker-compose.yml` (Dependencies Only)

```yaml
version: '3.8'

# Dependency Emulators for Kaizen Agent local development
# Start with: docker compose up -d
# App runs natively via: mise run dev -j2

services:
  # 1. BigQuery Emulator (Traceability & Telemetry queries)
  bigquery-emulator:
    image: ghcr.io/goccy/bigquery-emulator:latest
    container_name: kaizen-bigquery-emulator
    ports:
      - "9050:9050"
    command:
      - "--project=kaizen-local"
      - "--dataset=manufacturing"
      - "--port=9050"
    restart: unless-stopped

  # 2. Firestore Emulator (Blackboard shared state)
  firestore-emulator:
    image: gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators
    container_name: kaizen-firestore-emulator
    command: gcloud beta emulators firestore start --host-port=0.0.0.0:8086
    ports:
      - "8086:8086"
    restart: unless-stopped

  # 3. Pub/Sub Emulator (Sensor & Anomaly streaming)
  pubsub-emulator:
    image: gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators
    container_name: kaizen-pubsub-emulator
    command: gcloud beta emulators pubsub start --host-port=0.0.0.0:8085
    ports:
      - "8085:8085"
    restart: unless-stopped

  # 4. MQTT Broker (Factory sensor & conveyor telemetry)
  mosquitto:
    image: eclipse-mosquitto:latest
    container_name: kaizen-mqtt-broker
    ports:
      - "1883:1883"
    environment:
      - "ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true"
    restart: unless-stopped
```

### 2. "If I have this docker compose setup, do I still need the emulator above?"

**No, you don't need any additional emulator setup.**

Here is why:

1. **Docker Compose *is* running the emulators:**
   Running `docker compose up -d` (or `mise run docker:up`) spins up the exact emulator containers:
   - BigQuery (`ghcr.io/goccy/bigquery-emulator:latest` on `:9050`)
   - Firestore (`gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators` on `:8086`)
   - Pub/Sub (`gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators` on `:8085`)
   - MQTT Broker (`eclipse-mosquitto:latest` on `:1883`)

   You **do not need** to install `gcloud`, Java, or any emulator binaries on your macOS host machine.

2. **Simplified `mise.toml` commands:**
   - **Start all emulators:** `mise run docker:up` (runs `docker compose up -d`)
   - **Stop emulators:** `mise run docker:down`
   - **Start only BigQuery:** `mise run emulator` (runs `docker compose up -d bigquery-emulator`)

3. **Offline / No-Docker fallback remains intact:**
   If you don't even have Docker running, the code will still function by falling back to in-memory mock data automatically.
